description: ZeroRodCAD Desktop 2.0: the WebView gets no shell/process/broad-filesystem permission at all, per ADR-022-001's security boundary. It can only call the app's own narrow, app-registered commands (core:default) — M2 adds sidecar-lifecycle commands here, never a general shell/process grant. Build 024 M1 added dialog:allow-open, which lets the WebView ask the OS to show its native open/folder-picker dialog and receive back the single path the user chose; Build 025 M1 reuses it (unchanged) for the project-open file picker (tauri-plugin-dialog's ACL gates the whole 'open' command, not file-vs-folder pickers separately) and adds dialog:allow-save for the project Save As file picker. Neither grants message/ask/confirm dialogs, and — critically — neither grants filesystem read/write/list capability of its own; the WebView still cannot read a directory listing or a file's contents directly, only receive an opaque path string and hand it back to the Rust-owned engine_export/engine_project_open/engine_project_save commands, which are the only things that ever read/write bundled with a user-chosen path. Build 025 M1 native-close corrective fix adds core:window:allow-destroy: core:default only pulls in core:window:default, which does NOT include allow-close/allow-destroy, so the app's own documented onCloseRequested pattern (main.ts) — preventDefault() only to cancel, otherwise falling through to the JS wrapper's implicit destroy() once the unsaved-changes guard resolves 'proceed' — was being silently ACL-rejected at the final step. Tauri's native window-event handler (tauri::WindowEvent::CloseRequested) already calls the Rust-side prevent_close() synchronously whenever any JS close-requested listener is registered (so it can await the async guard), which is what made the red macOS close button hang indefinitely instead of closing: the native close was correctly deferred, but the deferred destroy() call that was supposed to resume it never had permission to run.
